data.why: The app's own EXAMPLES list and committed data/scaler.pkl + data/metrics.json cover the single-variant Predict page and the Performance page with no extra files; the written CSV (gene,hgvsp columns matching page_batch's required schema) gives the Batch page something to upload, including a bad gene, a malformed HGVSp token, and a missing value to exercise its error paths.

goals: Triage a single candidate missense variant (gene symbol + HGVSp) to get a pathogenicity probability and decide whether it warrants further workup
Compare a known pathogenic hotspot (e.g. TP53 p.Arg175His) against a likely-benign polymorphism in the same gene to sanity-check the model's calibration
Inspect the residue-level context of a mutation via the ±128-residue window and the AlphaFold 3D structure view, colored by distance from the mutation site
Batch-screen a CSV list of variants to produce a ranked/flagged shortlist for manual review, then download the results
Review the model's reported performance (accuracy, ROC curve, confusion matrix, top SelectKBest features) to judge how much to trust a given call

review.summary: The tree gets the purpose right (triage missense variants and judge how far to trust the model), its specific labels and the seven screens I checked are accurate, and the Performance and Batch phases are well built. But because nothing could be scored offline, it leaves out the actual result read-out and the 3D structure inspection that the README and code centre on, so it needs those added as not-reached tasks and features, plus some regrouping and wording fixes, before filing.
